tasks.short: Develop and implement cytogenetic training programs

steps.what: Identify trainees' needs and select current procedures and teaching examples
Develop the written training sequence and exercises

loop.input: Training brief with selected procedure sections, objectives and approved teaching examples
loop.output: Draft sequence and exercises linked to supplied sections
loop.check: Technologist checks scientific meaning, procedural order, example answers and trainee suitability in s3
loop.stop: One draft; unsupported claims or unsuitable exercises are rewritten manually within retained preparation time
loop.why_not_simpler: A native document outline supplies headings but does not adapt explanations and exercises to the supplied learning needs

steps.what: Check training accuracy, exercise answers and suitability before teaching
Save the checked material in the existing training folder
Implement training through demonstrations, supervised practice and feedback

tasks.design: Test the existing {DOCS} training outline first. For material that still needs individual explanations, use a bounded draft from a technologist-selected brief and retain scientific checks, repairs and all supervised practice.
tasks.previous_blocker: An outline does not explain specimen artefacts or adapt an exercise to a trainee's experience.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded drafting loop can work from selected procedure passages without choosing clinical procedures itself.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching safe bench practice and deciding whether a trainee understands an abnormal pattern.
tasks.human_edge: The trainer observes technique and corrects unsafe reasoning in context.
tasks.altitude: Some drafting time returns to demonstrations. Training responsibility and competence decisions stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Assessment design and the limits of shared laboratory procedures

evidence.claim: A bounded language-model draft can adapt explanations from supplied source passages, subject to expert correction; savings here are estimates.

assumptions: Boundary is developing actual program material and delivering it, not a new attendance register or competence certification workflow. Shares are provisional task estimates, not measured baselines.

The technologist produces the training brief in s1: learner level, learning objectives, procedure version, selected passages, exercise scope and approved synthetic or previously cleared teaching examples. Selecting and preparing these inputs remains fully counted.
No identifiable specimen data enter the drafting loop. Missing or unsuitable examples are handled manually; no free de-identification pipeline is assumed.

Native outlines are tried first. Only 9 of the 30 drafting hours are removed by initial wording and ordering; 21 remain for construction and correction, plus the separate 14-hour accuracy check. Ordinary save time is retained without a self-approval gate.

The material is used directly in supervised teaching. No machine release, invitation send or new record is claimed. Permissions and applicable national consultation requirements are checked during rollout.
unknowns: How much program material is newly written rather than reused unchanged?
Can approved examples be supplied without additional clearance work?
research_questions: Do corrected drafts preserve laboratory procedure order and technically correct exercise answers?

already_counted.description: Source selection, retained drafting repairs and scientific checks

incremental.description: Rechecking source versions and the drafting instructions as procedures change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: 30*30%=9 gross, less 2 upkeep gives 7. Low: hands-on training with already reusable written material offers no removable drafting; retain the current program and do not deploy the loop, with no new upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recognize cellular abnormalities and report verified findings

steps.what: Recognize abnormalities in cell color, size, shape, composition or pattern
Enter observed findings and specimen limitations in the laboratory case
Assemble the report from the recorded case fields
Check report meaning, specimen identity and limitations; repair assembly failures
Save the technically checked report as a draft
Authorize the final abnormalities report under the laboratory release procedure
Release the authorized report to the internal clinical result record

tasks.design: Configure a report template in the {OTHER} laboratory information system to assemble existing recorded findings and case identifiers. The technologist retains visual interpretation and technical repairs; the laboratory reviewer authorizes the final snapshot before clinical release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report assembly is often mixed with the skilled act of interpreting a specimen.
tasks.enabler_now: Native report fields can copy exact existing case values without generating clinical meaning.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing biological abnormalities from artefacts and communicating uncertainty accurately.
tasks.human_edge: Qualified staff relate morphology, preparation quality and case context.
tasks.altitude: Less report assembly, with unchanged interpretation and release responsibilities.

reach.task: Check a laboratory report template against recorded findings
reach.learn: Field provenance, report validation and release controls

evidence.claim: Laboratory report templates can assemble exact case fields while qualified staff retain interpretation and release; the proposed effort shares are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary starts with an identified specimen and its existing microscope or imaging view in {OTHER}; specimen preparation and image acquisition are unchanged laboratory work, with no saving credited. This task owns finding entry, report assembly and internal clinical release. Subsequent explanation to recipients is separate.

The technologist captures case identifier, specimen identifier, observation text, relevant counts, method, limitations and observation date in s2. The existing case request supplies patient identifier, requested test and specimen type. Missing fields are completed manually within s2 and s4.

The native template copies exact identifiers, observation text, method and limitations into the actual report. It does not infer a karyotype, classify cells or turn an unstructured observation into a diagnosis. All 20 assembly hours are removable only where this duplication exists today.

The 10 retained technical-check hours include manual reconstruction of failed or incompatible layouts and checking scientific meaning. The 8 reviewer hours belong to another role and do not enter the focal denominator. These are estimated shares, not measured throughput.

Saving an authored draft is ordinary retained work at s5 and has no approval gate. Clinical release is a consequential action at s7; authorization binds the exact report content and case identity, and any revision requires fresh review. No external send is performed here.
unknowns: Does the laboratory already assemble this report automatically?
Who has the local authority to authorize clinical release?
Which fields and layouts are available natively?
research_questions: Does the configured template preserve unusual limitations and prevent case-field mismatches?

already_counted.description: Finding capture, semantic verification and failed-layout repair
Laboratory review remains another role's existing work

incremental.description: Retest report field mappings and layouts after laboratory system changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact saved report content, case identifier and destination record in the s6 authorized snapshot; edits invalidate authorization

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Focal B=92, R=72: gross 21.74, less 2 upkeep gives 19.74. Low: an existing automatic report or unsupported image-only case fields remove none of today's assembly; retain the present workflow without new upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Communicate test results and technical information to authorized recipients

steps.what: Read released test results and establish the recipient's technical information need
Write the secure technical message accompanying the released report
Check final message meaning, disclosure permission, report version and recipient
Send the checked message and released report to the authorized external physician
Explain technical results and limitations and answer the recipient's questions

tasks.design: Use the {OTHER} laboratory system's secure-message template for repeated case identifiers and the report-version reference. Staff write the actual technical explanation, check the final disclosure and recipient, then send through the existing secure channel and answer questions personally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case headers and the substantive technical explanation are often treated as one writing task.
tasks.enabler_now: An existing message template can reuse exact case fields without interpreting the result.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining uncertainty and the limits of a test to a particular recipient.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist notices misunderstanding and stays within the role's scope when discussing clinical implications.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in repeated typing; authority and the recipient conversation stay unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a technically accurate explanation of test limitations
reach.learn: Accessible language and the boundary between laboratory explanation and counseling

evidence.claim: Secure-message templates can reuse exact case headers; they do not replace technical explanation or disclosure judgment.

assumptions: This communication episode includes an actual written technical response to an external physician and a follow-up conversation. The released report is an existing output of the laboratory reporting process, not produced free by a new model here. No reporting-assembly saving is counted again.

The existing laboratory record supplies case identifier, released report identifier and version. In s1 the technologist checks the information request, verified recipient identity, disclosure permission and permitted communication scope. Missing permissions or addresses stop the send for manual resolution within retained checking time.

The native template removes only 2 of 20 writing hours: repeated identifiers and the report-reference header. The other 18 hours retain all bespoke explanation, actual source reading, repairs and ordinary draft saving. The 1-hour real send remains fully retained.
The s3 check binds message content, attachment version, recipient and disclosure scope before the real send. Any change voids it. It is a disclosure gate, not a gate on the author's ordinary save.

No transcript, communication log or new report is added. If the real episode is solely a call, there is no invented message baseline and this template offers no saving. Shares are unmeasured scenario estimates.
unknowns: How many episodes include a written message rather than only a call?
Are case headers already filled in the secure channel?
Which recipients may this role contact directly?
research_questions: Does the message template preserve the correct report version without causing disclosure or interpretation errors?

already_counted.description: Request reading, substantive message writing, disclosure checks and recipient clarification

incremental.description: Check the secure-message header and report-reference template after changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact technical message, released-report attachment version, verified recipient and disclosure scope checked in s3; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: 20*10%=2 gross, less 0.5 upkeep gives 1.5. Low: a phone-only episode or a secure channel that already fills the case header leaves no duplicate typing; retain the current workflow without a new template or upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated report assembly and limited training drafting while keeping microscopy, scientific checks and communication with qualified staff.
reach: Help laboratory colleagues validate report field provenance
Prepare clearer explanations of test limitations with a genetic counselor
role.ambitious_version: A technologist who spends more preparation time on difficult specimens and supervised teaching, with unchanged clinical decision rights.
